_comment: Shahnama of Firdausi, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V: Zarduhst's coming, the war of religion, Asfandiyar's dragon stage. Paraphrase passages with notes.

title.en: Zarduhst Appears with Fire from Paradise
title.zh: 扎爾杜什特持天堂之火顯現

region.en: Palace of Gushtasp at Balkh (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 巴爾赫古什塔斯普王宮（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Gushtasp secs. 2-4

summary.en: A Tree appeared on earth within the palace of Gushtasp and grew up to the roof, a Tree whose roots spread far and wide, whose leafage was precept and its fruitage wisdom, a Tree right fortunate and named Zarduhst, the slayer of malignant Ahriman. I am a prophet and thy guide to God, said he, and brought a censer filled with fire: this have I brought with me from Paradise; the Maker said take thou this, and look upon the heaven and the earth, because I made them not of dust and water. When the good Shah had heard of that good Faith, his valiant brother Zarir and all the mighty chiefs assumed the cincture and received the Faith; he set up Fanes of Fire and first established the Fire of Mihr Barzin, and Zarduhst planted the noble cypress of Kishmar before the portal.
summary.zh: 一棵神樹在古什塔斯普宮中生長至屋頂——其根深廣、其葉為訓、其果為智——此樹名扎爾杜什特，「誅滅惡神阿赫里曼者」。「我是先知，是你通神的引路人。」他捧著盛火香爐：「此火我自天堂攜來；造物主說：『天地非由塵水所造——看這火焰便知我的創造。』」賢王與弟扎里爾及群臣繫上聖帶、皈依真教；王遍設火廟，首立米赫爾·巴爾津聖火，先知於火廟前植下基什馬爾神柏。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the coming of Zoroaster in the Shahnama. Prophet-vision cluster; handle as literature. No living community restriction.

passages.text: Thus passed a while, and then a Tree appeared on earth within the palace of Gushtasp, and grew up to the roof, a Tree whose roots spread far and wide, a Tree with many branches, its leafage precept and its fruitage wisdom: how shall one die who eateth of such fruit? A Tree right fortunate and named Zarduhst, the slayer of malignant Ahriman. Thus said he to the monarch of the world: I am a prophet and thy guide to God.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: He brought a censer, filled with fire, and said: this have I brought with me from Paradise. The Maker of the world said: take thou this, and look upon the heaven and the earth, because I made them not of dust and water: behold herein how I created them. See now if any one could do this thing, save I that am the Ruler of the world? If thou acknowledgest My handiwork thou must acknowledge Me to be the Lord. Receive His good religion from the speaker, and learn from him His usage and the way; see that thou do as he directeth thee, choose wisdom, recognise this world as vile, and learn the system of the good religion, for kingship is not well when Faith is lacking.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: When that good Shah had heard of that good Faith, and had accepted it and its good customs, his valiant brother, glorious Zarir, who used to vanquish mighty elephants; the Shah, his father, now grown old at Balkh; the mighty chiefs from all the provinces, the wise physicians and the men of war, all gathered to the monarch of the earth, assumed the cincture and received the Faith. Then was the Grace of God made manifest, for evil left the hearts of evil men. Then mounting to his throne high-born Gushtasp dispatched his troops throughout the provinces, distributed archmages through the world, and set up Fanes of Fire: he first established the Fire of Mihr Barzin. Zarduhst then planted him a noble cypress before the portal of the Fane of Fire, and wrote upon that noble, straight-stemmed tree: Gushtasp is convert to the good religion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 3 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Zarir Falls to Bidirafsh's Treacherous Dart

region.zh: 阿亞斯戰場（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Gushtasp sec. 14

summary.en: Zarir, brother of Gushtasp, rides into the enemy camp like blazing fire and wind amid the grass, and none that beheld withstood him. Arjasp, astound, offers his daughter's hand and the conduct of his host to whoever will throw the maddened Elephant from his steed, and at last the lusty Bidirafsh advances, that foul dog, that warlock, that old wolf. Adventuring not to face him openly, the enchanter skirmished round him stealthily and hurled unseen at him the double-headed dart: his royal mail was pierced, his kingly form bedrenched with blood, and he tumbled from his steed. Woe for that youthful, royal cavalier!
summary.zh: 古什塔斯普之弟扎里爾如烈火疾風般衝入敵營，所向披靡。阿爾賈斯普驚惶許諾：誰能將那頭狂象掀下馬，便以公主相許、授予兵權！最終那「惡犬、術士、老狼」比迪拉弗什應聲而出——不敢正面交鋒，卻繞行偷襲，暗中擲出雙頭鏢：王甲洞穿、君軀浴血，英雄墜馬。哀哉，那年輕的王族騎士！

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the war of religion cycle (Ayas = Khwarazm). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Then brave Zarir advanced before the host, bestriding his huge chestnut, threw himself upon the encampment of the enemy, like blazing fire and wind amid the grass, slew, and dispatched them to their last repose: none that beheld withstood him. Then Arjasp, perceiving that the prince had slaughtered many of name, cried loudly to his warriors: the warriors of Shah Gushtasp have slain full many a man of name among our troops, and now Zarir is in the midst of you, as 'twere a fierce wolf or a rending lion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: We must devise a remedy for this, or trudge back to Turan, said Arjasp; what man of you in quest of fame will go forth man-like, alone, and compass world-renown? I will bestow on him my daughter's hand, and give to him the conduct of my host. The soldiers answered not a word, for all feared that Wild Boar. At last the lusty Bidirafsh advanced, the foul, that dog, that warlock, that old wolf, and spake thus to Arjasp: O mighty Sun! I will confront yon raging Elephant; if I shall seize and fling him to the dust before the king, let me be leader of this countless host.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: That foul enchanter with the loathly form went toward Zarir, the leader of the folk, but seeing from afar his fearsome fury, his beard besoiled, his eyes fulfilled with dust, a mace like Sam the hero's in his hand, and slain before him heaped up like a mountain, adventured not to face him openly, but skirmished round him stealthily and hurled unseen at him the double-headed dart. His royal mail was pierced, his kingly form bedrenched with blood. He tumbled from his steed. Woe for that youthful, royal cavalier! Foul Bidirafsh alighted, stripped the prince, and bare off to the king the horse and girdle, the standard and the goodly, jewelled crown.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 14 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.zh: 納斯圖爾與阿斯凡迪亞爾誅比迪拉弗什

region.zh: 阿亞斯戰場（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Gushtasp sec. 17

summary.en: Nastur, the slaughtered prince's son, rides forth on his father's Bihzad: Nastur am I, the offspring of Zarir; where is that warlock Bidirafsh who holdeth the flag of Kawa? Bidirafsh comes on wearing Zarir's mail and wielding the selfsame sword wherewith he had overthrown Zarir; seeing Asfandiyar advance, he hurled his baneful weapon at the prince to darken that radiant face: it missed the prince, who caught it in his hand and pierced, a hero's stroke, his foeman's liver, so that the point came out the other side. Thus Bidirafsh fell from his steed and perished, and Asfandiyar, stripping off the armour of Zarir from that ancient warlock, severed the head and brought back to the Shah the prince's dun steed.
summary.zh: 扎里爾之子納斯圖爾騎父親的比赫扎德出陣：「吾乃扎里爾之子！那竊取卡瓦戰旗的術士何在？」比迪拉弗什披著扎里爾的鎧甲、持那把弑主的寶劍而來；見阿斯凡迪亞爾逼近，擲出毒鏢欲遮其光輝容顏——王子接鏢在手，一擊貫穿其肝！術士墜馬而亡；阿斯凡迪亞爾剝其甲、斬其首，牽回父王的坐騎與戰旗。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; blood-vengeance episode. No living community restriction.

passages.text: The Shah then gave his steed Bihzad, his helm of steel, and sable breastplate to Nastur, the slaughtered prince's son who, armed and mounted, rode forth between the opposing hosts and, halting before the battle of the enemy, heaved from his breast a deep, cold sigh, and cried: Nastur am I, the offspring of Zarir: the lion dareth not encounter me. Where is that warlock Bidirafsh who holdeth the flag of Kawa?
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: Then Bidirafsh went forth at once, he bare the violet flag, was mounted on the charger of prince Zarir, and wore the prince's mail, advancing in his pride toward Nastur. Men told the glorious Asfandiyar, the Shah's son, of their combating, who made all haste to go to them. Now when that chief of sorcerers beheld this, and perceived what man now was advancing to assail him, he urged his charger from amid the fray, and hurled his baneful weapon at the prince to darken if he might that radiant face.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: It missed the prince, who caught it in his hand and pierced, a hero's stroke, his foeman's liver, so that the point came out the other side. Thus Bidirafsh fell from his steed and perished, experiencing the might of Kaian birth. Asfandiyar dismounted from his steed, and stripping off the armour of Zarir from that ancient warlock, whose head he severed from its trunk withal, he carried off the prince's glossy charger, the flag, and head of worthless Bidirafsh. The Kaian army raised a shout: the prince hath triumphed, hath overthrown the foe, gone forth, and brought the dun steed back!
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Gushtasp sec. 17 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

title.en: Asfandiyar and the Dragon in the Sword-Box
title.zh: 阿斯凡迪亞爾劍匣鬥龍

region.en: Stages on the road to the Brazen Hold (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 通往銅堡的路上（象徵性定位）

source.work: Firdausi, Shahnama, trans. A. G. & E. Warner (1905), vol. V, Seven Stages sec. 4

summary.en: Gurgsar warns the prince of an awesome dragon whose breath doth draw forth from the deep the fish, a flame of fire proceeding from its maw, its body a mountain made of flint. Asfandiyar has carpenters build a wooden carriage all set about with swords and a box, harnessed two noble steeds, and drives at the dragon; the horses strove to 'scape its mischief, but it sucked them in, them and the break, and in his box dismayed the warrior: in the dragon's gullet stuck the sword-blades, and blood poured forth like a sea. Tortured by the points and chariot the dragon by degrees grew weak, and the gallant warrior, arising from the box, hacked the dragon's brains till fumes of venom overpowered him and he tumbled mountain-like and swooned away.
summary.zh: 古爾格薩爾示警：前方有巨龍，「呼氣可自深海引出遊魚，口吐烈焰，軀如燧石之山」。王子命木匠造一輛四面插劍的木車、附一座劍匣，親坐其中，驅雙駿直衝巨龍；駿馬欲逃卻被連車吸入口中——龍喉被劍刃卡住，鮮血如海湧出；魔龍受刺與車磨，漸漸力竭；王子自匣躍出，如獅狂斫其腦，直至毒煙熏得他如山傾倒、昏厥於地。

sensitivity.note: Epic literary source; the Seven Stages of Asfandiyar (Haft Khan counterpart of Rustam's). No living community restriction.

passages.text: Gurgsar returned reply: gone hast thou into battle like a fire, and made a shift to over-pass these bales, but know'st not what will come on thee tomorrow; there will encounter thee an awesome dragon, whose breath doth draw forth from the deep the fish; a flame of fire proceedeth from its maw; its body is a mountain made of flint. Asfandiyar replied: thou evil one! I mean to drag thee in thy chains with me to be a witness that this sharp-clawed dragon escapeth not my trenchant scimitar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: At his command some carpenters were fetched, and therewithal some long and heavy beams. He had a goodly wooden carriage built all set about with swords and with a box, and harnessed to the break two noble steeds. Afar the dragon heard the rumble and beheld the prancing of the battle-steeds; it came like some black mountain, and thou wouldst have said: the sun and moon are darkened. Its two eyes seemed fountains bright with blood, while from its gullet fire issued, and like some dark cavern gaped its jaws.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.

passages.text: It bellowed at Asfandiyar, who, seeing the monster, drew his breath and turned to God for help. The horses strove to 'scape the dragon's mischief, but it sucked them in, them and the break, and in his box dismayed the warrior. In the dragon's gullet stuck the sword-blades, and blood poured forth like a sea; it could not free its gullet, for the swords were sheathed within it. Tortured by the points and chariot the dragon by degrees grew weak, and then the gallant warrior, arising from the box, clutched his keen glaive with lion-grip and hacked the dragon's brains till fumes of venom rising from the dust overpowered him; he tumbled mountain-like, and swooned away.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Firdausi, Shahnama, Seven Stages sec. 4 (Warner 1905); not verbatim.
